overall: New York City hit a daily high of 100.0°F at 13:52 ET and has been in a clear cooling phase for roughly 5 hours, now sitting at 96.1°F with zero upward velocity. An Extreme Heat Warning remains in effect through July 4, but today's peak is almost certainly already in the books. The day unfolded as a classic extreme heat event — rapid morning ramp, early-afternoon peak, steady cooling thereafter.
forecast_obs_notes: The major NWP models (GFS=104.4°F, ECMWF=104.2°F, HRRR=102.6°F) significantly overshot the observed max; NBM at 100.6°F was the closest to reality. The NWS text forecast of 100°F verified almost perfectly. Model spread was moderate on the high side, and the NBM/NWS consensus proved far more reliable than the global dynamical guidance today.
max_temp_prediction: With the running max locked at 100.0°F since 14:50 ET, temperatures actively declining for 5 hours, clear skies (no convective trigger to produce a late heat burst), and wind staying light out of the west, the final TMAX is essentially certain to be 100.0°F. In the active odd-bucket Kalshi market the relevant bucket is 99-100F, not the ensemble-model-favored 95-96F bucket — the intraday observation supersedes the prior model distribution entirely. Confidence is very high (near-certain) given the observed and locked running maximum.
